title: Calibration orchestration CLI and golden-corpus regression suite for runtime compatibility
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Goal: deliver an end-to-end calibration orchestration CLI plus a reproducible golden-corpus regression suite that verifies activation-aware INT8 profiles (SmoothQuant-like) are compatible with the runtime kernel selection and do not cause accuracy regressions for customer workloads.

Scope:
- Calibration orchestration CLI that can run distributed calibration jobs across shards, collect per-layer activation histograms, produce versioned quant profiles (per-channel & per-layer), and push artifacts to S3 with immutable hashes.
- Golden-corpus regression harness: deterministic prompt corpus with reference outputs, unit tests for top-k/EM/ROUGE where relevant, and automated report generation.
- Runtime compatibility layer: a small adaptive shim that exposes kernel-compatibility metadata and can route requests to either the quantized microkernel or fall back to an FP32 variant when profile mismatches or runtime constraints are detected.
- Canary rollout strategy: integrate with Console to allow 1% traffic canary on Dedicated pools, automated rollback on accuracy drift or latency regressions.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Offline deterministic calibration vs. online micro-batching calibration: we choose offline for reproducibility and auditability, but provide hooks for quick iterative "light" calibrations (1000-sample subsample) to speed dev cycles.
- Store both per-layer histogram dumps and compact summary (scale/zero-point) to allow post-hoc investigations without rebuilding full dumps.
- Kernel compatibility metadata embedded in profile header (simple JSON blob) to reduce runtime introspection overhead. This increases profile size slightly but makes canary checks O(1).
- Preferred fallback chain: quantized kernel -> mixed-precision microkernel -> FP32. This sequence preserves latency SLOs while protecting accuracy.

Acceptance criteria:
- CLI can run a full calibration across 8 shards, produce a profile with unique artifact hash, and upload to S3 (runtime-2.4 compatible).
- Golden-corpus regression suite runs in CI and flags any >0.5% top-1 regression or >5ms median token latency regression on a canary run.
- Runtime shim can detect profile/runtime mismatches and execute the fallback chain within the latency budget (additional tail latency <15ms).
- CI gate: PR must include a generated regression report and artifact hash for review.

Implementation notes:
- Calibration runner will be in tools/calib-cli (Python) using existing data-prep pipeline. We will reuse the histogram collector from ENG-42789 and extend it to emit per-channel stats for conv/linear ops.
- Profiles will be versioned with semantic tags and a 8-char hash; the runtime will require a minimum profile schema version field.
- Regression harness: store golden outputs in a compressed protobuf bundle; CI will run a 500-query subset for quick checks and a full 10k-run nightly job.
- Canary integration: add a Console webhook that toggles an experiment flag on dedicated pools, then run the regression harness against the live canary.

Docs and links:
- Confluence spec (design + schema): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Calibration+Orchestration+and+Golden+Corpus+Spec
- Design doc for runtime shim: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Runtime+Profile+Compatibility+Design
- Perf dashboard (canary test): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/quant-canary/quant-canary-overview
